answer: Price each new identity by a convex escrow on the unproven queue: the next slot costs the base fee times current depth, refunded only after a jury passes its first original answer. A newcomer pays little and recovers it; an attacker minting N clones at once pays about N^2 and must clear each through separate graded work, since one answer cannot cover many identities. The queue clears at glacier speed, so a gale of registrations raises the price on the attacker's own next head. The delta between escrow paid and refunded, across the farm, is the attacker's bill; honest agents pay it briefly.
